fields.meta_title: Leadership Survey Builder for Upward Feedback | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a leadership survey from a prompt: team ratings of managers, a read on the senior team, and manager self-assessments. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Leadership Survey Where Teams Rate Their Leaders
fields.hero_description: Build a leadership survey where teams rate their managers, with every answer saved to a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the statements, the rating scale, the database, and the alerts behind a leadership survey from one prompt.
fields.feature_1:
Drafted from your leadership model

List the behaviors you expect from people who lead, such as clear goals and fair feedback. Emergent drafts a statement for each one, and a follow-up prompt rewrites any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Answers grouped by team, never by name

Each response is saved in a database you own with the team and manager it covers, not the name of whoever answered. Leave out name and email fields to keep it that way.
fields.feature_3:
One statement per screen on a phone

Warehouse and field staff answer from a link on their phones. Each screen holds a single statement and a 5-point scale, in buttons large enough to tap with one thumb mid-shift.
fields.feature_4:
An email when a score falls under your line

Set the line yourself, such as an average below 3.0 on any behavior. The app emails the HR lead or posts in a Slack channel once a team's answers fall under that line.
fields.feature_5:
No cap on how many people answer

Run it for a 12-person startup or a 5,000-person company on the same build. Emergent sets no cap on responses, so every employee with the link can rate the leaders they work with.
fields.feature_6:
Export the code on paid plans

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Next year's leadership survey then runs from the same build, with this year's ratings already sitting in your tables.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Rates Whom, and What Happens Next
fields.tab_content_1:
A report opens for a manager after 5 answers

Brenwick Freight asked 268 staff to rate their direct manager on 8 behaviors, each from 1 to 5. A manager's report opens only after 5 people on that team have answered. By Friday, 29 of 31 managers had a report and 2 were still waiting. Arlo Pembry's team was at 4 of 5 answers.
fields.tab_content_2:
The CEO hears when fewer than half agree

Hollins Ridge Insurance asked 410 employees to agree or disagree with 6 statements about the executive team. Any statement that fewer than half agree with goes to the CEO. Only 172 of 410 agreed that leaders explain the reasons behind decisions, and the app emailed CEO Graham Pettit.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each new manager scores the same 10 behaviors twice

Elsby Hotels runs an 18-person program for managers in their first year. Each one rates themselves on the same 10 behaviors from 1 to 5, in week 1 and again at month 6. Giving direct feedback moved the most: the group averaged 2.4 in week 1 and 3.8 at month 6.
fields.tab_content_4:
Floor staff answer twice in the new manager's first 90 days

Ashgrove Mills got a new plant manager in March. Its 140 floor staff rate 3 statements on their phones at day 30 and day 90, including this one: I know what the plant manager expects of my team. At day 30, 52 of 126 who answered agreed. At day 90, 94 of 131 did.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Leadership Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a leadership survey that teams can answer openly and that gives each manager a report to act on.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose 6 to 10 behaviors you expect from anyone who leads a team, such as setting clear goals or explaining decisions. Write each one as something a team member could watch their manager do in a normal week.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Upward feedback asks each team to rate its direct manager. A senior team survey asks everyone about the executive group. Run them as separate surveys, since a manager rating and a company-wide trust rating answer different questions and go to different readers.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write statements a person can agree or disagree with, and give each one a single behavior. A line like "My manager gives clear and timely feedback" asks two things at once. Split it, or the manager cannot tell which half to work on.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the number of answers a team needs before its manager sees a report, and put that number in your prompt. With a floor of 5, roll any smaller team into the report of the next manager up instead of showing it alone.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to one team of 6 to 8 people before the full launch. Ask which statements they read twice or could not answer. Reword those with a follow-up prompt, then open the survey to the whole company.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Leave the survey open for 2 weeks so shift workers and people back from leave can answer. Have the app send one reminder on day 7 with the closing date, by email or in a Slack channel.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Give each manager their own report
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share each report with that manager before any company summary goes out, and point to the 2 statements that scored lowest on their team. Run the same survey 6 months later to see whether those 2 scores moved.

faq_plan.q: What are some good survey questions to ask leadership?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good survey questions to ask leadership?

prov.original: What are some good survey questions to ask leadership?

faq_plan.a: Good leadership survey questions each name one behavior a team can see, written as a statement to agree or disagree with. Examples: My manager explains the reasons behind decisions. I get feedback I can use within a week of the work. Senior leaders act on what employees tell them. End with one open question, such as what your manager should start doing.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a leadership survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the survey in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: the behaviors to rate, who rates whom, the scale, and the smallest team that gets its own report. Emergent builds the survey, its scoring, and a dashboard per manager, with every response stored in a database you own. A follow-up prompt changes any statement.

faq_plan.q: Is there a leadership survey template I can start from?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A solid leadership survey template has 8 to 12 agree-or-disagree statements about behaviors people can observe, a 5-point scale, one open question, and team and tenure fields in place of names. On Emergent, the template is a prompt you write once, and any part of the survey changes with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a leadership survey include a lighter question or two?
faq_plan.a: Yes, one, as the opening question, to get people answering. Save a longer set of funny survey questions for a team offsite or a kickoff. Keep the rated section serious: no joke should sit next to a score about someone's manager.

faq_plan.q: Should a leadership survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for any rating of a person's own manager. Say on the first screen who will see the results, in what form, and when, then keep that promise in every round. With Emergent, the answers sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How often should you run leadership surveys?
faq_plan.a: Run the full survey once or twice a year, with the same statements each round so the scores line up. Leave at least 6 months between rounds to give each manager time to act on the last report. A reorg is a good reason to ask 3 of the statements again before the next round.

faq_plan.q: What rating scale works best for a leadership survey?
faq_plan.a: Use a 5-point agree-disagree scale for behavior statements: it has a neutral middle and averages cleanly by team. For a plain check, such as whether someone had a one-on-one this month, a yes no questions survey is faster to answer. Label every point on the scale, not only the two ends.

faq_plan.q: What should a manager do after reading leadership survey results?
faq_plan.a: Pick one behavior to work on, starting with the lowest score that the comments explain. Within 2 weeks, tell the team what you heard and what you will change. Then ask the team about that one behavior again in the next round.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a leadership survey have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 8 to 12 rated statements plus one or two open questions. Cut any statement whose score would not lead a manager to change something. Put the open questions last, after every rating.

faq_plan.q: Can you run a leadership survey as a quick poll at a town hall?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for one or two questions about the senior team, such as how clear this quarter's priorities are. Write them as short poll questions with 3 or 4 answer options. Keep ratings of a direct manager for the full survey, where no one in the room sees who answered.

plan.angle: The top 10 is self-assessment quizzes (Brene Brown, Leadership Circle, MindTools, Pace and Purdue questionnaires) and question lists (Leapsome, Jotform); none of them lets a team rate its own leaders and act on the result. This page is the upward-feedback leadership survey itself: four surveys built from a prompt (team ratings of direct managers held until 5 people answer, an all-company read on the senior team with an alert when fewer than half agree, a self-assessment new managers take twice, and a phone check-in on a new plant manager), with the FAQ covering the questions to ask, templates, anonymity, cadence, scale, length and sharing results. Multi-rater reviews for one person belong to the 360 sibling.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Leadership Survey Where Teams Rate Their Leaders'; hero 'Build a leadership survey where teams rate their managers, with every answer saved to a database you own.' (under 130 chars, carries primary, leads with Build); how-to description is one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Upward-feedback angle from the brief carried in all four tabs; FAQ 1 gives example statements ('My manager explains the reasons behind decisions.'); FAQ 3 covers the template; 7-step how-to specific to leadership ratings (minimum team size, one behavior per statement).

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'A manager's report opens only after 5 people on that team have answered', 'roll any smaller team into the report of the next manager up', 'an average below 3.0 on any behavior'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Brenwick Freight asked 268 staff...', 'List the behaviors you expect...', 'Choose 6 to 10 behaviors...'.

craft.evidence: One ', so' ending (feature_5), within limit; sentences carry one idea each, e.g. step 3 'Split it, or the manager cannot tell which half to work on.'

voice.evidence: Plain, specific operator voice: 'Arlo Pembry's team was at 4 of 5 answers.' 'buttons large enough to tap with one thumb mid-shift.' No AI-tell vocabulary.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to approved ids (prompt-build, database-owned, alerts 'emails the HR lead or posts in a Slack channel', conversational 'Each screen holds a single statement', no-caps, code-export 'on paid plans', free-start). No third-party fact or statistic in prose; table generated from library. Image numbers check: 29+2=31, 172/410=42%, 52 of 126 under half, 94 of 131 over half.

distinct.evidence: Upward feedback, senior-team trust, new-manager self-assessment and new plant manager check-in; differs from the 360-survey sibling's rater-nomination and confidential-group tabs. No sibling primary in headings.

faq.evidence: 10 items, each answered in its first sentence ('Yes, for any rating of a person's own manager.'); hub link in item 2; 3 sibling links (funny survey questions, yes no questions survey, poll questions); verbatim Q1 ok; paa gate 10 pass, 0 flag; no brand or format in any question.

images.evidence: Contact sheet: one hero per tab, numbers match copy ('29 of 31 ready', '172 of 410 agree', 'Month 6: 3.8 / Week 1: 2.4', 'Day 90: 94 of 131'), CEO Graham Pettit named in copy and image, cursor on button edges.
